# Jambukhādaka Saṁyutta (SN 38)

**ID:** SN 38
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Jambukhādaka Saṁyutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0304m.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Jambukhādakasaṁyutta* (SN 38) is the thirty-eighth section of the *Saṁyuttanikāya*, situated within the *Saḷāyatanavagga* [Bodhi 2003b; Nyanaponika & Bodhi 2003]. It comprises sixteen discourses recording questions put to the Venerable Sāriputta by the wanderer (*paribbājaka*) Jambukhādaka, whom the commentary identifies as Sāriputta's nephew, while Sāriputta was dwelling in Magadha at Nālakagāma [Bodhi 2003a; Bodhi 2003b; Nyanaponika & Bodhi 2003; Hazra 1994]. The wanderer asks Sāriputta about fundamental doctrinal themes, including the nature of extinguishment (*nibbāna*), arahantship, those who proclaim the Dhamma, the goal of the holy life, consolation (*assāsa*), feeling, ignorance, the taints (*āsava*), personality (*sakkāya*), and the difficulty of practicing the Dhamma [Bodhi 2003a; Bodhi 2003b; Nyanaponika & Bodhi 2003]. Throughout these dialogues, Sāriputta repeatedly defines both *nibbāna* and arahantship as the destruction of lust, hatred, and delusion (*rāgakkhaya*, *dosakkhaya*, *mohakkhaya*), declaring the Noble Eightfold Path to be the path leading to their attainment [Hazra 1994; Nyanaponika 1986; Wen 2011]. In SN 38.16 (*Dukkarapañhāsutta*), Sāriputta identifies practice in accordance with the Dhamma (*dhammānudhammappaṭipatti*) as the most arduous undertaking in the teaching [Wen 2011]. Discussing SN 38.1, the commentary (*Sāratthappakāsinī*) clarifies that *nibbāna* is not merely the temporal destruction of the defilements, but the unconditioned element apprehended through the supramundane path contingent upon which defilements are eradicated [Bodhi 2003b; Nyanaponika 1986].

 Parallels and citations from the *Jambukhādakasaṁyutta* are also preserved in the Tibetan Tanjur [Nyanatusita 2013], and DharmaNexus identifies cross-language textual alignments with several portions of the Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 99, fascicles 14, 18, 28), the *Madhyamāgama* (T 26), the Sanskrit *Arthaviniścayasūtra* and Harivarman's *Tattvasiddhiśāstra*, and Tibetan commentaries such as Śamathadeva's *Abhidharmakośopāyikā-ṭīkā* (D 4094) and the *Abhidharmasamuccayavyākhyā* (D 4054) [DharmaNexus].

- [Bodhi 2003b] Bhikkhu Bodhi, Connected Discourses of the Buddha: A New Translation of the Samyutta Nikaya (2003) — Details the 16 suttas, identity of structure with SN 39, list of questions to Sāriputta, and commentarial gloss on Nibbāna in note 271.
- [Nyanaponika & Bodhi 2003] Nyanaponika Thera, Hellmuth Hecker, and Bhikkhu Bodhi, Great Disciples of the Buddha: Their Lives, Their Works, Their Legacy (2003) — Identifies Jambukhādaka as Sāriputta's nephew and summarizes the topics of SN 38.1–16.
- [Hazra 1994] Kanai Lal Hazra, Pali Language and Literature (1994) — Summarizes Sāriputta's dialogue with Jambukhādaka defining Nibbāna and arahantship as destruction of lust, hatred, and illusion.
- [Wen 2011] Tzungkuen Wen, A Study of Sukkhavipassaka in Pali Buddhism — Cites SN 38:2 on arahantship and SN 38:16 on practice according to the Dhamma being the most difficult task.
- [Nyanaponika 1986] Nyanaponika Thera and Erich Fromm, Vision of Dhamma: Buddhist Writings of Nyanaponika Thera (1986, 2000) — Quotes SN 38:1 and discusses Buddhaghosa's commentarial refutation of Nibbāna as mere destruction of defilements.
- [Nyanatusita 2013] Bhikkhu Nyanatusita (ed.), The Bodhisattva Ideal: Essays on the Emergence of Mahayana (2013) — Cites Peter Skilling's study on three citations from the Tibetan Tanjur with parallels in the Jambukhādaka-saṁyutta.
